title: Patient-Centered Treatment Planning for Chronic Multimorbidity: A Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning Framework for Preference Modeling
abstract: arXiv:2609.39911v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Patient preference, defined as a patient's demonstrated willingness and capacity to adhere to clinical recommendations, is a primary determinant of therapeutic effect yet remains structurally absent from existing computational treatment planning models. We address this gap by presenting patient-centered factored-action hierarchical option-critic (FAHOC), a hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) framework that jointly learns high-level options corresponding to therapeutic strategies and factored intra-option policies that decompose the joint action space into disease- and intervention-specific subcomponents, while imposing a cooperation-aware action masking mechanism. This enables structured exploration, improved credit assignment across hierarchy levels, and more interpretable decision pathways, while enforcing patients' preferences. Formal guarantees establish that cooperative patients achieve higher optimal expected health outcomes

translated_title: 以患者为中心的慢性多病共存治疗方案规划：一种用于偏好建模的分层强化学习框架
translated_abstract: 患者偏好，定义为患者对临床建议表现出的依从意愿与能力，是治疗效果的主要决定因素，然而在现有的计算化治疗规划模型中却存在结构性缺失。为填补这一空白，我们提出了以患者为中心的分解动作分层选项-评论家框架（FAHOC），这是一种分层强化学习（HRL）框架，联合学习与治疗策略相对应的高层选项，以及将联合动作空间分解为疾病特定与干预特定子组件的分解式选项内策略，同时施加一种合作感知的动作掩码机制。这使得结构化探索、跨层级的信用分配改进以及更可解释的决策路径成为可能，同时能够强制执行患者的偏好。形式化的理论保证表明，合作型患者可以获得更高的最优期望健康结果。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种以患者为中心的分层强化学习框架FAHOC，通过联合学习治疗策略选项与分解式选项内策略，并引入合作感知的动作掩码机制，首次将患者偏好纳入慢性多病共存治疗规划的计算建模中，同时提供了合作患者可获得更优健康结果的形式化保证。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes FAHOC, a patient-centered hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that jointly learns therapeutic strategy options and factored intra-option policies with a cooperation-aware action masking mechanism, for the first time incorporating patient preferences into computational treatment planning for chronic multimorbidity, with formal guarantees that cooperative patients achieve higher optimal expected health outcomes.
